title: Article 106 — Salaries and allowances of members

content.overview: Article 106 provides that members of either House of Parliament shall be entitled to receive such salaries and allowances as may from time to time be determined by Parliament by law and, until provision in that respect is so made, allowances at such rates and upon such conditions as were immediately before the commencement of this Constitution applicable in the case of members of the Constituent Assembly of the Dominion of India.
content.glance: MP salaries and allowances: determined by Parliament by law; interim rates as for Constituent Assembly members pre-commencement.
content.study:
Article 106 authorises Parliament to determine salaries and allowances of members of both Houses. Until such law, transitional rates linked to the Constituent Assembly applied.

Examination: parliamentary power; transitional baseline.

sections.heading: Key rule
sections.body: Salaries and allowances of members of either House: as determined by Parliament by law; until then, as applicable to Constituent Assembly members immediately before commencement.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How are salaries of members of Parliament fixed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 106, members of either House of Parliament are entitled to such salaries and allowances as may from time to time be determined by Parliament by law. Until such provision is made, the rates and conditions applicable to members of the Constituent Assembly of the Dominion of India immediately before commencement applied.

examTips: Parliament by law fixes MP salaries and allowances.

keyTakeaways: Art 106: MP salaries/allowances fixed by Parliament by law.
